figure: FIGURE 23.1 (From vague ask to architectural bounds), caption vs drawing
issue: The caption claims the dialogue 'surfaces the six architectural numbers in Table 23-1 (traffic & concurrency, token profile, SLO, quality bar, option, TCO)', but the figure shows no quality bar at all, and the numbers it does show do not map one-to-one onto the six named categories (the figure carries TTFT p95 2.1 s, an SLO triple, 9.2K-token prompts, 8xH100 and ~$14.6K/mo, and a scope list). The caption therefore promises a mapping the figure does not exhibit.

What is the true problem? ... TTFT p95 2.1 s on a 70B model'; '2. What does success look like? p95 TTFT <= 2 s, ~25 ms/token, 40 rps peak'; '3. figure: FIGURE 24.1 (Red Team / Green Team cycle) — caption
issue: Probable digit/letter typo in the caption: severity classes are written 'any Po/P1 finding blocks promotion; P2/P3 are tracked but non-blocking' — 'Po' (letter o) where the scheme requires 'P0' (zero), inconsistent with the adjacent 'P1/P2/P3'.

The same caption renders P1, P2, P3 with clear digits; the 'o' in 'Po' is round and o-height. Could not be resolved beyond doubt at 150 dpi — this may be a glyph-rendering artifact rather than a source typo, so it is filed at P3 pending a source check. Figure body itself is semantically consistent with the caption (7 numbered steps 1–6 plus feedback leg; '1→6 forward cycle; one red feedback loop back to step 1' matches the drawn red return path from box 6 to box 1; the probe→exposure→guardrails→metrics→green-team order in the caption matches boxes 2→3→4→5→6).
acceptance_test: Grep the source for 'Po/P1'; if the character is a letter o, replace with 'P0'; re-render and confirm the caption reads 'any P0/P1 finding blocks promotion'. If the source already contains 'P0', close as a render artifact.

issue: The '6 Green Team' box is blue, while '1 Red Team' is red. The diagram's title and labels use team color names, so the color encoding contradicts the label. A reader scanning by color sees no green team.
evidence: Box 1 is dark red and labeled '1 Red Team'; box 6 is blue and labeled '6 Green Team'; no green box appears in the cycle.
acceptance_test: Render the Green Team box in green (or a neutral color) and keep Red Team red; verify grayscale distinguishability and that the label/color mapping is consistent.

issue: The six stage boxes are distinguished only by hue (dark red, red, orange, purple, teal, blue). In grayscale, boxes 2, 4, 5 and 6 collapse to similar mid-tones, and the red feedback loop becomes a mid-gray line of similar weight to the black forward-flow arrows. The figure survives only because each box carries a number and a label; the color carries no redundant information. This is a weaker encoding discipline than the one used elsewhere in the book (FIGURE 26.1 uses hatch patterns as well as color).
evidence: Printed 364: boxes '1 Red Team' (dark red), '2 Probes' (red), '3 Exposure' (orange), '4 Guardrails' (purple), '5 Metrics' (teal), '6 Green Team' (blue); forward arrows dark, feedback loop red. Compare printed 384 (FIGURE 26.1), where each series carries a distinct hatch ('/', 'x', '.').
acceptance_test: Add a redundant non-color encoding to the six stage boxes (e.g. distinct hatch density, or a shape/weight difference), or confirm on a grayscale print proof that the numbered labels alone are sufficient and that the feedback loop remains distinguishable from the forward arrows by routing and weight.

issue: The caption names the fifth field 'Alternatives considered (the rejected options)', but the figure's box label is 'Alternatives' (sub-label 'rejected options'). The field name in the caption should match the figure exactly.

issue: The composition is left-heavy: the five-field stacks occupy a narrow column at the left while roughly the right half of the figure area is empty except for the two centered record titles and one italic annotation. issue: The figure's central causal claim - that the Consequences of ADR-001 become the Context of ADR-002 - is asserted by a text label rather than shown by the drawing. The dashed red connector runs from the ADR-001 horizontal rule down to the ADR-002 horizontal rule in the empty space to the right of the field stack; it does not touch the ADR-001 'Consequences' box or the ADR-002 'Context' box. evidence: Printed 374 figure: dashed red vertical arrow between the two horizontal rules, with the label 'consequences of ADR-001 become the context of ADR-002' placed to its right; the five field boxes ('Title & status', 'Context', 'Decision', 'Consequences', 'Alternatives') are stacked at the left of both records. acceptance_test: Draw the connector from the ADR-001 'Consequences' box to the ADR-002 'Context' box (a routed elbow that visibly terminates on both boxes), or add explicit field-level markers (e.g. a 'becomes' tag on the ADR-001 Consequences box and a 'from ADR-001' tag on the ADR-002 Context box). Verify on the rendered page that the connector's endpoints touch the two named boxes.

issue: The chart occupies only the vertical middle of the page, leaving a large empty band above the title and below the footnote (excessive whitespace / poor vertical balance). The figure and its caption are not balanced on the page.

figure: FIGURE 26.1 (Workload fingerprints on the six axes)
issue: The figure title and the surrounding prose call the six categories 'axes', but the chart has one value axis ('Authored intensity (0-1)') and six categorical groups. 'Six axes' implies a six-dimensional space (which is what the parenthetical 'grouped bars, not radar' is implicitly disclaiming), and the prose on the facing page repeats the phrase: 'the six axes (context length, traffic, quality required, cost sensitivity, latency sensitivity, output tokens)'. 'Six dimensions' or 'six workload characteristics' would be exact.
evidence: Printed 384 figure title: 'Workload fingerprints on six axes (grouped bars, not radar)'; y-axis 'Authored intensity (0-1)'; x-axis categories 'Context length', 'Traffic (rps)', 'Quality required', 'Cost sensitivity', 'Latency sensitivity', 'Output tokens'. Printed 383 prose: 'the six axes (context length, traffic, quality required, cost sensitivity, latency sensitivity, output tokens) are subjective normalized scores (0-1)'.
acceptance_test: Use 'six dimensions' (or 'six workload characteristics') consistently in the figure title, the facing-page prose, and the note, and confirm no remaining sentence in the book describes these as axes of a multidimensional space.

issue: Operator inconsistency between figure labels and caption, and within the FACT box itself: the figure prints exact-looking values ('baseline TTFT p99 450 ms', 'TTFT mean 180 · p99 250 ms', 'utilization 45%') while the caption hedges the same values with '~' ('~180 ms', '~250 ms', '~450 ms uncached baseline'); the FACT box mixes operators in one block ('request rate ~2 rps' has '~', 'utilization 45%' and '450 ms' do not). Because the box is headed '1 · FACT', unqualified numbers invite a measured-data reading the [ILLUSTRATIVE] caption is at pains to deny.
evidence: Figure FACT box: 'request rate ~2 rps / utilization 45% / baseline TTFT p99 450 ms'. Figure DERIVED box: 'TTFT mean 180 · p99 250 ms'. Caption: 'mean TTFT ~180 ms and p99 TTFT ~250 ms (−44% vs the ~450 ms uncached baseline ...)' and 'Scope: ... [ILLUSTRATIVE] conceptual'. Arithmetic checks out ((450−250)/450 = 44.4% ≈ 44%, p99-to-p99 as caption states), so the defect is operator/label discipline, not the numbers. Arrow labels and directions are otherwise correct: FACT→DERIVED 'trace', DERIVED→PATTERN 'validate', PATTERN→FACT 'adjust + pick pattern'/'feedback' with arrowhead entering FACT from below, matching the caption's FACT → DERIVED → PATTERN forward path.
acceptance_test: Add '~' to the figure's 450/180/250/45% labels (or add 'illustrative, rounded' to the FACT/DERIVED box headers) so figure operators match the caption's '~' operators; confirm no exact-valued number remains in the figure where the caption prints '~'.

issue: The '1 · FACT' node lists 'request rate ~2 rps / utilization 45% / baseline TTFT p99 450 ms' as if they were gathered FACTs, but the prose of the same capstone (PDF 410 / printed 390, Step 1) explicitly states these are 'assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTs (R-07): no author-run load test produced them ... not a measured runtime quantity a FACT would be.' The figure therefore mis-scopes assumed inputs as measured evidence, violating the book's own evidence-label discipline (R-07 / Ch. 4 axis taxonomy).
evidence: Fig 26.2 box 1 header reads '1 · FACT' with body 'request rate ~2 rps / utilization 45% / baseline TTFT p99 450 ms'. Page 410: 'These are assumed baseline inputs, not gathered FACTs (R-07) ... They become FACTs only once instrumented and recorded in a genuine load test.' The 450 ms is the assumed service-time sum 320+80+50, described on 410 as 'a scenario input, not a derived quantile of a distributed sample.'
acceptance_test: Relabel the node so it does not present the assumed 2 rps / 45% / 450 ms as gathered FACTs — e.g. split it into a 'READ: workload fingerprint' FACT node (short prompt, latency-sensitive, moderate quality) plus an 'ASSUMED BASELINE' node for the 2 rps / 45% / 450 ms, or rename the box 'INPUTS (assumed baseline)'. After the change, a reader comparing the figure to page 410 must find no statement that the 450 ms or 2 rps is a measured FACT.

issue: The DERIVED node states 'decode bandwidth-bound' as a clean conclusion, but the prose (page 410, Step 2) hedges it: 'batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there.' The figure drops the conditionality, risking the exact 'decode is always bandwidth-bound' misconception the book warns against.
evidence: Fig 26.2 box 2 body: 'decode bandwidth-bound' (no qualifier). Page 410: '...so decode lands in the bandwidth-bound regime (the low-batch regime of Ch. 8; batch size, context precision, kernel, and hardware decide whether it stays there).'
acceptance_test: Add a short qualifier to the DERIVED node (e.g. 'decode bandwidth-bound (low-batch regime)') or a footnote marker tying it to the page-410 conditionality, so the figure no longer reads as an unconditional law.
